R0256.title: Crowdsourced Same-Triplet Order Splitting
R0256.definition: In crowdsourced delivery, groups split orders sharing the same sender, recipient, and address to fraudulently claim delivery fees and subsidies.
R0256.description:
Crowdsourced same-triplet order splitting exploits identical sender, recipient, and address (the "three identicals") to split one order into multiple sub-orders, claiming per-order delivery fees, subsidies, and bonuses.

The risk causes multiplied delivery-fee and subsidy leakage and distorts capacity dispatching. Detection must combine same-address clustering, splitting timing, and delivery-trail linkage to merge settlement and recover benefits.
R0256.influence: The risk causes multiplied delivery-fee and subsidy leakage, distorts capacity data, and crowds out legitimate couriers' order rights.

references.title: Case of defrauding nearly one million yuan in food-delivery subsidies (Legal Weekly, crowdsourced order-splitting arbitrage)
Heytea store manager colluded with delivery riders to defraud 130000 yuan in delivery fees (NetEase, crowdsourced order-splitting arbitrage case)

observables: Crowdsourced orders show split-order patterns with identical sender, recipient, or address
A single order is split into multiple sub-orders to farm per-order delivery fees
Same-address send-receive clusters show anomalously concentrated split-order timing
Delivery fees and subsidy payouts are anomalously high for specific riders or stations
Post-split delivery trajectories show the goods are actually the same shipment
